snip.t: Any one of: fasting plasma glucose 7.0 mmol/L or more; 2-hour glucose 11.1 mmol/L or more on a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test; HbA1c 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) or more; or a random glucose 11.1 mmol/L or more with classic symptoms.
Diagnosis: Elevated IGF-1 levels and lack of GH suppression by an oral glucose tolerance test.

qs.q: A patient with suspected acromegaly has elevated growth hormone levels that fail to suppress during an oral glucose tolerance test. What is the normal physiological response being tested?
o: Hyperglycemia triggers hypothalamic somatostatin release to inhibit GH
Glucose directly binds pituitary receptors to stop transcription
Insulin surge activates JAK-STAT pathways to degrade circulating GH
High serum osmolarity alters portal blood flow to the adenohypophysis
Suppression occurs via direct pancreatic feedback loops on somatotrophs
qs.e: Oral glucose normally suppresses growth hormone secretion via hypothalamic somatostatin release in healthy individuals, an effect lost in acromegaly.

qs.q: During a glucose tolerance test, plasma glucose rises significantly, yet all filtered glucose is initially reabsorbed. What accounts for this complete reabsorption up to a threshold?
qs.e: Glucose reabsorption relies on secondary active symporters that have a finite transport maximum, leading to saturation at high loads.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Physiology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 29-year-old woman at 35 weeks gestation undergoes a routine urinalysis which demonstrates 1+ glucose, despite a normal random blood glucose level and a negative oral glucose tolerance test. What is the mechanism for this finding?
o: Primary renal tubular acidosis affecting bicarbonate handling
Urine sample contamination with high molecular weight proteins
Parathyroid hormone-related peptide altering distal nephron function
Filtered glucose load exceeding tubular reabsorption capacity
qs.e: Glycosuria is common in pregnancy because the increased GFR presents a filtered glucose load that exceeds tubular reabsorption. This occurs independently of gestational diabetes.

qs.q: The oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) uses a glucose load of ---
qs.e: The standard oral glucose tolerance test uses a 75‑gram glucose load.

qs.q: An adult presents with enlarged hands and feet, jaw prognathism, and glucose intolerance. Laboratory tests show GH >1 ng/mL after an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) and elevated IGF-1. What is the diagnosis?
qs.e: Acromegaly is caused by excess GH secretion after epiphyseal closure. The diagnostic criteria include failure of GH suppression to <1 ng/mL after a 75g OGTT and elevated IGF-1. Clinical features include prognathism, macroglossia, and acral enlargement.
